findings.reason: a node that maps the seeded memory through `_display_state` alone passes both cases and ships the raw-vs-word defect §6 exists to remove, for four of the seven words; the second case must assert each seeded seven-word input renders that exact word on the left.
findings.text: the second done-when case checks only that rendered left words fall "among the seven", which does not distinguish an identity mapping from one that blanks a word: `_display_state(delivered/halted/landed/dropped)` returns "" (verified), and a blanked `from_state` renders a row with no left word, so the plan never requires a seeded seven-word input to render as itself and the first case seeds only `working`, which already maps to itself — the deliverable's stated requirement that those four words map to themselves is therefore unmeasured
